text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong spells out the People's Action Party's 'Singapore 21' vision.
- Singapore People's Action Party to have its candidates draw detailed plans to improve wards.
- Thailand's New Aspiration Party leader General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh forms coalition with five other smaller parties after official results showed it won most seats in general election.
- Fewer large Housing Development Board resale flats change hands in third quarter.
- Singapore's non-oil domestic exports for last month expected to decline by 1.3 percent.
- Six local banks jointly launch Singapore Regional Index Fund.
- Thailand's stock market dive 5.8 percent on concern over poll results.
- Manufacturing and distribution group Ossia International's initial public offering 15.4 times subscribed.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says government will act if growth slows further.
- Malaysia Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad accuses Britain's Midland Bank of not accepting cheque from national car manufacturer Proton and blocking its acquisition of British sports car maker Lotus.
- Specialist construction firm Wee Poh Holdings launches initial public offering of 24.8 million shares at Singapore 45 cents each.
- Malayan Credit in talks to buy another Grange Garden site for Singapore $85 million.
- Singapore Telecom shares fall on Morgan Stanley Capital International index news but later end unchanged.
